label: early-position input bigram (prev in q/f/a/e/y/c/v/o/3, current in d/a/c/q/y) at t=1-2
explanation: Most of the activation mass (about 75%) falls in the original phase at t=1 (52%) and t=2 (21%). It never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, at orig positions 4 and up, or at recall_idx 0. Whether it fires depends on the recent input bigram: the current input is d, a, c, q or y (lift 3-5x) and the previous input is q, f, a, e, y, c, v, o or 3. Top examples are o q [d], o q [a], 3 q [d], with prev2 o/3. The largest activations (about 0.14 of a 0.16 max) are on o q d / o q a. The predicate gets about 0.79 precision at t=1 alone but misses many weaker bigram combinations. The remaining ~24% of mass is in the copy phase, spread across recall_idx 2-5. There it is enriched when the output is o or z, and it re-fires on inputs that repeat an early bigram (e.g. x [g] after the delimiter), but that part is diffuse and adding it lowers precision. Overall it looks like a nonlinear readout of the first two tokens and is not captured by one simple clause.
